title: #redwood #redwoodmusical #redwoodbroadway #redwoodbway #idinamenzel #...
transcript: The wickedly talented Idina Menzel is back on Broadway in a new musical called Redwood. Based on the marketing materials, I went into this thinking it was basically gonna be “middle aged woman at a crossroads in life climbs a tree to find herself” And honestly, that's pretty accurate so big props to the marketing team. Now, the downside here is that this premise kind of struggles to sustain what's currently a two hour one act. I’m willing to get behind the show being primarily a vehicle for Idina and the rest of the stellar cast, but I found the material kind of hard to invest in. The score is overall pleasant and certainly contains some gems, such as a really fantastic performance by Zachary Noah Piser toward the end of the show. But I also felt like a good amount of the score was somewhat forgettable, or just not vital to the storytelling. And with very little dramatic conflict or tension in the first half, it really meanders for a while before getting to the root of it, pun intended. But with the show still in early previews, I think there's an opportunity to prune and give it more focus. From a visual perspective, this has some really impressive video and projection designs, and pretty much the whole stage is a huge screen. I loved how immersive it felt, even from the rear mezz, and how that effect is used to portray Idina’s character Jesse's thoughts and, in a way, put the audience in her mind. I think if you're a fan of Idina or a sucker for cool visuals, you should definitely check this one out. But, respectfully, it's still very much cooking, so if I were you, I'd put it on my radar for closer to opening night. With that, another playbill for my collection.
reasoning: The reviewer gives a balanced assessment with both positive elements (praising Idina Menzel, cast, visuals) and significant concerns (pacing issues, forgettable score, lack of dramatic tension). The recommendation is conditional - suggesting fans of Idina or visuals check it out, but advising general audiences to wait until closer to opening night when issues might be resolved.
